canonical_statement: For every natural dimension n and complex-valued function f on R^n, f is represented by a mathlib SchwartzMap exactly when f is infinitely differentiable and, for every polynomial weight k and Frechet-derivative order r, the weighted derivative norm is uniformly bounded.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; EuclideanDomain n := Fin n -> Real; f : EuclideanDomain n -> Complex; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: for every k and r there is a uniform real bound on norm(x)^k * norm(iteratedFDeriv Real r f x)
conclusion: Existence of a complex-valued SchwartzMap with underlying function f is equivalent to the smooth rapid-decay conditions.
checked_transport_relationship: Existential function-level membership is equivalent to inhabitation of the subtype of bundled SchwartzMap representatives with underlying function f.

killed: required decay only for the function rather than every derivative

degenerate_cases: Dimension zero is retained. No nonzero-function or positive-bound premise is imposed; the zero function and constant zero-dimensional functions remain within the characterization.
